summary: The electric GLB replaces the EQB as Mercedes-Benz's seven-seat electric SUV, built on the same MMA platform and 800-volt hardware as the CLA and sold here in two grades, the rear-drive 250+ and the dual-motor 350 4MATIC, both with an 85kWh usable battery and seven seats standard. Australian reviewers rate it well: CarExpert calls it one of the most enjoyable mainstream Mercedes SUVs in recent memory and Chasing Cars says it finally deserves the badge, though both find the screen-heavy cabin and haptic controls polarising and the third row fit only for children. It undercuts the outgoing EQB by more than $15,000, which makes it a value pick among premium seven-seat EVs rather than a true seven-adult carrier.
pros: At $74,990 before on-road costs the 250+ is the cheapest seven-seat electric SUV here and sits just $10 under the $75,000 cap that keeps the full FBT exemption from 1 April 2027; the 350 4MATIC at $86,200 stays under the $91,661 LCT threshold
85kWh usable battery gives 570km (250+) and 554km (350 4MATIC) WLTP on the standard 20-inch wheels, and Chasing Cars measured 15.7kWh/100km in the 350 4MATIC, about 541km real-world
800-volt architecture charges at up to 320kW DC, 10-80 per cent in a claimed 22 minutes
Reviewers praise the ride: Chasing Cars found 'hugely improved ride quality' over the EQB and CarExpert called it 'easily one of the most enjoyable mainstream Mercedes-Benz SUVs'
Five-year unlimited-kilometre warranty, eight-year/160,000km battery cover, and a 127-litre front boot on top of the rear load space
cons: The third row suits occupants under 171cm only, and with all seven seats up the boot shrinks to 145 litres (480 litres with the third row folded)

Interior divides reviewers: Chasing Cars marks down the polarising dashboard screens, flawed haptic steering-wheel controls and quality 'not quite premium', and CarExpert says there is too much screen
CarExpert lists 'ridiculous servicing costs' among its criticisms of the new GLB
Efficiency claims vary in testing: CarExpert's European drive of the 250+ used 18.1kWh/100km, near the top of the claimed band, for roughly 470km per charge
Not yet rated by ANCAP or Euro NCAP, and Mercedes EV resale here has been weak, with this car itself launched more than $15,000 below the EQB it replaces
